title: Keep a Two-Gigabyte Upload off the API
description: A video app's API servers spend most bandwidth proxying uploads. The service still needs to authorize each file and track its owner. Which split fits?

options.text: Make the bucket publicly writable and let clients choose any key.
options.explanation: That removes authorization and allows writes outside the intended file scope.

options.text: Put each video in the metadata database row.
options.explanation: Large database blobs inflate backups, replication and buffer-cache pressure without removing the transfer problem.

options.text: Keep uploads in API memory until the user finishes.
options.explanation: That keeps bandwidth and long-lived state on the API fleet and loses progress on crashes.

options.text: Authorize metadata in the API and issue a short-lived URL for direct upload to a chosen object key.
options.explanation: The API controls ownership and permission while object storage handles bytes. Completion still needs server-side verification and cleanup of partial outcomes.
